records.sections: Chapter 3: pp46–50 preparation; pp51–58 manual setup; pp58–64 thermal setup; AGC pad p56/p62
records.scope: Exact 1 GHz GainMaker HGD module family; verify installed split and conventional OEM control option. Not ACI DSIM. HGD 42/54 MHz catalog profile.
gaps: Historical manufacturer-authored manual on a third-party mirror. A newer exact installed-module revision was not publicly recovered; confirm module, split and applicable procedure before adjustment.

The guide describes an analog video pilot. OEM QAM detectors also exist, but this review did not recover an exact detector setup/offset bulletin. Confirm installed detector part number, pilot type, frequency and level convention. A -6 dB datasheet loading relationship is not an AGC correction.
Manual-backoff and thermal setup are alternatives for the same fitted OEM AGC. Select the locally approved method; do not combine the two.

procedureModes.label: Manual backoff → OEM AGC
steps: Match the installed RF module, split, OEM AGC detector and design print; record approved low/high frequencies, output levels, tilt, pilot and loading.
Confirm valid input at both design frequencies and allow approximately one hour warm-up. Add 20 dB to raw -20 dB test-point readings only if the meter has not already compensated.

Before setting levels: S1 = 2 (manual setup). Turn MANUAL BACKOFF fully counterclockwise, then clockwise by the exact system amplifier p53 temperature/reference-frequency chart amount. Do not readjust backoff afterward.
At the main output, compare high-minus-low level with design tilt. Increase input EQ if tilt is low; decrease it if high. Remeasure.
At the highest design frequency, adjust forward input pad to the approved output: a larger pad lowers level; a smaller pad raises it. Recheck level and tilt.
Verify every output against its design reference. HGD/LGD auxiliary test points are after the signal director; account for director loss only when the print specifies a before-director level.
For the applicable conventional OEM detector, install AGC pad = corrected MAIN output pilot level (dBmV) minus 34 dB. Do not use an auxiliary-port level; confirm pilot compatibility first.
Record the corrected main-output pilot level in S1 = 2. Select S1 = 3 and adjust AGC GAIN to reproduce that level.
Toggle S1 between 2 and 3, allowing the module to settle before each reading. Repeat AGC GAIN adjustment until switching causes no level shift; the guide gives no fixed settling time.
Leave S1 = 3. Verify approved levels/tilt and each output again, record pilot/control/pad/EQ and before/after readings, then continue the job’s separate return workflow.

steps: Match the installed RF module, split, OEM AGC detector and design print; record approved low/high frequencies, output levels, tilt, pilot and loading.

Record the corrected main-output pilot level in S1 = 1. Select S1 = 3 and adjust AGC GAIN to reproduce that level.
Toggle S1 between 1 and 3, allowing the module to settle before each reading. Repeat AGC GAIN adjustment until switching causes no level shift; the guide gives no fixed settling time.

procedureModes.label: Thermal: amplifier only
steps: Match the installed RF module, split, thermal control configuration and design print; record approved low/high frequencies, output levels, tilt, pilot and loading.

Leave the selected thermal operating mode active. Record control mode, pad/EQ, corrected levels and before/after evidence; continue the separate return workflow.

records.title: AOI Quantum18 HGD / HGBT · setup · historical original-manual mirror
records.sections: Chapter 1 pp3–6 identity/splits/test points; Chapter 3 pp38–43 preparation/profile; pp44–46 downstream; pp47–48 upstream; p49 ALSC; p50 test-point routing
records.scope: Quantum18 GainMaker-form-factor HGD and HGBT only. The manual lists 85/105, 204/258, 396/492, 492/606 and 684/834 MHz splits; match installed diplex modules, firmware and profile. Does not apply to LE, BA, MB or BLE.
steps: Match HGD/HGBT and physical diplex split. Connect QuantumLink Local to the intended interface. Check About for interface firmware/app version/MAC, then Amplifier Info for the installed device identity (pp38–40).

In Amplifier Config, match the displayed split to the installed diplex modules and confirm 1.8/1.2 GHz operating mode and active firmware bank. The guide starts ALSC OFF; enable only after both alignments below (p41).

Choose the intended measurement path under Test Points → Test Point Operation. Main FWD IN selects FWD IN or REV OUT; main/aux FWD OUT selects FWD OUT or REV IN. Add 20 dB to a raw -20 dB test-point reading only if the meter has not already compensated (pp6,50).

Confirm approved port output, marker frequencies, tilt and loading. In DS Auto Config, enter and verify the downstream profile marker frequencies and power levels, then Apply to store the profile. Confirm the actual approved pilots are present (p43).
After the profile is stored, select DS Align → Auto → Start Downstream Alignment. Verify the result before proceeding; this guide does not give a fixed AGC settling timer (p44).

Use downstream Manual only after Auto is complete and only if needed. Change one gain/tilt value at a time, apply with the checkbox, then Save Configuration to persist it. Revert restores the preset (p45).
Use Spectrum to check the resulting downstream response and approved output levels. Its roughly 30-second acquisition is a spectrum scan time, not an AGC wait instruction (p46).

After downstream balancing of the cascade, begin manufacturer upstream alignment at the last amplifier. Auto uses Upstream → Auto → Start Auto; save a successful alignment or revert and resolve it (p47).

If using manufacturer upstream Manual, this revision specifies ONX-630 DOCSIS Expert. Match instrument/firmware and the approved local return reference; adjust one value, apply, then Save Configuration (p48).

After both downstream and upstream alignment, open Amplifier Config and turn ALSC ON at each amplifier. Recheck levels, save configuration/evidence and complete the applicable local sweep acceptance (p49).
gaps: Newest public exact HGD/HGBT I&O located: V02102025. The manufacturer now offers installation guides by request, so this review cannot establish that it is the latest issued revision.
The previous original AOI PDF URL returned HTTP 404 on November 10, 2026. This working link is a third-party mirror of the original manual, clearly identified by title/revision.

records.title: Cisco GS7000 GainMaker Scaleable 4-Port Node Installation and Operation Guide
records.revision: OL-29643-02; Cisco support index updated October 12, 2017
records.sections: Chapter 4 pp95–112: forward pp107–110; reverse pp111–112. Appendix A pad/EQ charts; SM/LCM module discovery described in Maintenance and EDR appendix.
records.scope: Exact original Cisco PDF fully retrieved through Parallel in this refresh. Latest matching base hardware guide located in current Cisco support index remains OL-29643-02 (listing October 12,2017). Standard 1002MHz optical node only; installed launch module, receiver and FCM/RCM determine applicability.
steps: Match the 1GHz launch module, optical receiver, FCM/RCM routing, split and design print; check power and terminate unused RF ports per the manual (pp95–107).

Under the approved service procedure, clean/inspect optical connections, measure receiver input and choose the receiver attenuation switch from its exact table (pp107–108). This can interrupt service.
Measure the receiver RF output and the selected launch-port output. Add only uncorrected test-point coupling once; the standard node RF references are −20dB (pp108–110).
Set the OIB receiver pad for the highest required port level or independent segment; increase FWD PORT OUT pads to reduce other ports sharing that segment (pp108–110). Use actual design levels.
Select linear EQs for the installed 2-way or 4-way launch path and required tilt, then recheck both markers and all affected ports (pp109–110; Appendix A).

Use the matching analog-transmitter or EDR reverse procedure and approved receive reference. The SM/LCM Auto Set-Up button discovers installed modules; it does not perform RF level/tilt AGC alignment.
gaps: The manual uses 3.25% OMI and 50.2dBmV at1002MHz as an example; do not populate universal targets or pads from it.
Standard node manual balancing is different from Intelligent-node electronic AGC. A receiver attenuation switch is not a pilot-controlled RF AGC module.
Some extracted step cross-references are internally inconsistent; the workflow summarizes functional order rather than copying erroneous step jumps.
Do not use the analog-transmitter pad examples for an installed RPD or a different optical transmitter. Match its own setup guide.

records.title: Cisco 1.2 GHz GS7000 Node Installation and Operation Guide

records.sections: Chapter4 starts p85; forward pp93–95; reverse pp96–97; forward routing pp98 onward; Appendix A equalizer/pad charts.
records.scope: Exact original standard 1218MHz segmentable-node PDF fully retrieved through Parallel. Current support index still lists this matching base hardware guide. Keep standard optical, SHO/Fiber Deep, Intelligent and retrofit-RPD configurations separate.
steps: Identify standard1218MHz launch module, split, standard/low-input optical receiver and forward/reverse segmentation; verify power, unused-port termination and design targets (Chapter3; p93).
Measure optical input and apply the receiver-specific attenuation table on p94. Do not borrow the 1GHz receiver switch settings; check the original table at range boundaries.
Measure receiver RF output and launch-port levels; account for uncorrected −20dB RF test-point coupling once. The p94 receiver example is conditional on its OMI and optical level.
For the chosen segment, establish the highest required output using its OIB receiver pad, then use individual FWD PORT OUT pads to lower other shared ports (pp94–95).
Choose each path’s linear EQ from the1.2GHz chart to match the design tilt and remeasure the markers. Its factory18dB54–1218MHz tilt is a hardware reference, not a job target (p95).

For an active reverse path, select the procedure for the actual analog transmitter/EDR/RPD and approved receive reference; record all ports. Conventional LCM Auto Set-Up is module discovery, not RF balancing.
gaps: The 54dBmV@1218MHz/2.5%OMI forward example and15dB OIB pad are conditional examples, not universal launch settings.
Analog return example onpp96–97 is not a204MHz RPD receive target or XPERTrak acceptance procedure.
Standard85/102MHz datasheet specifies forward performance from105MHz; do not silently model102–105MHz as covered.
Installed firmware/options and native RPD conversion kits remain unidentified.

records.title: Cisco 1.2 GHz Super High Output GS7000 Node Installation and Operation Guide
records.revision: First published August 2016; support index August 18, 2016
records.sections: Chapter 3 p31; Chapter 4 p55; forward p60; reverse p63
records.scope: Original manufacturer SHO/Fiber Deep optical-node guide retrieved in full. Latest matching manual located remains August2016; current Cisco support index still links it. Applies only to its SHO launch and installed optical/RPD configuration.
steps: Confirm the SHO launch module, split, receiver type and return segmentation; complete Chapter3 power/termination checks (pp31–54).
Measure optical input, inspect/clean connections under the approved service procedure and use this manual’s receiver-switch table (pp60–61).
Measure receiver RF output at its−20dB test point and the highest required port; set the OIB pad from actual receiver drive and design output (pp61–62).
Reduce lower-level ports with their FWD PORT OUT pads. Set common EQ for overall tilt and left/right EQs for pair-specific tilt, then verify both markers (p62; Appendix A).

Use the installed analog/EDR/RPD return procedure. For the documented optical transmitter, p63 distinguishes4x1 and4x2 routing and the unused XMTR2 load; confirm actual configuration before changing it.
After module replacement, LCM Auto Set-Up discovers modules. It is not the Intelligent-node forward AGC setup.
gaps: Factory tilt conflict: module description and2017 datasheet accessories say21dB; setup p62 says22dB with common10.5dB and left/right12dB EQs. Verify installed response; do not create a universal factory target.
54dBmV@1218MHz and15dB OIB padding are conditional manual examples, not operator design targets.
Do not substitute standard segmentable or Intelligent electronic-control instructions.

records.title: Cisco GS7000 Super High Output Intelligent Node Installation and Operation Guide
records.revision: Cisco support index March 23, 2018; chapter update March 21, 2018
records.sections: Theory of Operation: RF Amplifier Module, AGC and Auto-setup; Setup and Operation chapter
records.scope: Original manufacturer hardware guide and software setup chapters retrieved. Latest matching hardware guide located is March2018; newer remote management guide24.1 is separately listed. Exact OIB/iRPD/LCS/manager versions must match.
steps: Identify Intelligent launch/OIB/iRPD and compatible software; confirm iRPD online, downstream carriers present and operator targets before auto setup.
Use the LCS RF Configuration screen to enter low/high MHz and corresponding dBmV for each required port, enable ports and Save. At least Port1 must be configured, enabled and saved.
Return to Node Configuration and start Auto Setup. This adjusts forward OIB drive; it does not align the return path.
After completion, check Auto Setup/AGC status and alarms; allow several minutes for AGC and compare each port’s internal spectrum with its saved targets.
Capture final per-port readings/settings and repeat forward setup when input levels materially change, following the installed-release procedure.
gaps: There are no physical forward/return RF amplifier test points on this Intelligent module. Use internal spectrum capture; never automatically apply a standard-node−20dB correction.
LCS instructions are detailed in the separate software guide. The hardware guide’s AGC describes independent electronic output level/tilt control per forward port.
Do not apply analog optical-receiver pad tables or standard node LCM module-discovery behavior as Intelligent RF alignment.
